absent: Watermark value computation and fast versus slow watermark check internals
Queue removal, page preparation, deferred growth, and memory acceptance helpers
Node dirty, reclaimability, and zone-eligibility predicate definitions
Compaction engine, suitability test, deferral reset, and priority constant values
OOM killer, OOM lock ownership, and progress signaling semantics
Direct reclaim core loop, kswapd wakeup, and pfmemalloc reserve policy
Full layouts of zonelist, zone, pglist_data, alloc_context, capture_control, and oom_control
Ordering between filesystem reclaim, memory stall, delay accounting, and interrupt contexts beyond the observed bracketing

findings.text: Fast allocation walks the caller supplied zonelist from the preferred entry, skipping zones that fail cpuset, dirty-spread node health, remote locality under no-fragment mode, or kswapd-idle preference, then evaluates watermarks and attempts to dequeue and prepare a block of the requested order. If no zone yields a page it retries once without kswapd skipping and once without the no-fragment restriction before reporting failure.

Watermark handling caches the below-high condition in a zone flag to keep the free path cool, selects the watermark level from the allocation flags, and on failure may attempt conditional memory acceptance, deferred zone growth, unrestricted watermark bypass, or node-local reclaim followed by a recheck before moving to the next zone. Remote-zone detection under no-fragment mode clears that restriction and restarts the scan to favor locality over fragmentation avoidance.

Conditional acceptance has two builds: one is inert and always declines; the other declines when the unaccepted list is empty or locking is forbidden, accepts a single large block when promotional watermarks are uninitialized, otherwise accepts enough large blocks to reach the promotional watermark after discounting unusable and already unaccepted free pages. Acceptance is probed before watermark checks and retried after dequeue failures.

Single-page acceptance serializes the unaccepted list with the zone lock held with interrupts saved, removes the first entry if present, then delegates to an accept helper that is documented to release that lock. Empty list handling releases the lock and reports no progress.

Node reclaim targets at least the requested order size or a cluster minimum, configured for file and slab reclaim with caller-derived blocking context, zone index, fixed priority, and mode-controlled write and unmap permissions. It refuses when reclaimable cache and slab are below node minima, when blocking is disallowed or the caller is already in emergency allocation, when the node has CPUs but is remote, or when another reclaim already holds the node reclaim bit.

Cpuset fallback performs a first freelist attempt with cpuset enforcement enabled and, only if that yields nothing, performs a second attempt with the caller flags unchanged, thereby ignoring cpuset placement when allowed nodes are exhausted.

OOM-path allocation first marks no progress, then tries to take the global OOM lock; contention marks progress, sleeps briefly, and returns empty. Under the lock it retries the freelist at very high watermark without direct reclaim, then declines OOM handling for coredump, costly high order, retry-mayfail or node-pinned requests, low zones, or suspended storage. Otherwise it invokes the OOM killer and, on success or nofail warning, marks progress and for nofail requests retries with watermarks bypassed.
Maximum direct-compaction retries for the retry policy is sixteen.

Direct compaction for costly-capable builds promotes the compaction order to cover a full pageblock for non-movable no-fragment requests, skips order zero, publishes a capture control for the requested zone and migratetype under memory-accounting and reclaim guards, runs compaction, then unpublishes before sampling any captured page. A captured page forces success status, is prepared, or is replaced by a freelist retry; skipped or deferred compaction returns empty without stall accounting, otherwise stall, success, or failure events are recorded. The alternate build always reports skipped and returns empty.

Compaction retry policy declines order zero and fatal-signal contexts. Skipped compaction retries only if the zonelist remains suitable; successful compaction allows bounded retries with a reduced budget for costly orders; failed compaction steps priority down toward a cost-dependent floor and resets the retry count. The compaction-disabled build instead retries only for non-costly orders while any zonelist zone satisfies its minimum order-zero watermark.

Synchronous reclaim wrapper yields the processor, records cpuset memory pressure, enters filesystem-reclaim and no-reclaim accounting around a direct reclaim call over the caller zonelist and nodemask, then restores accounting, yields again, and returns the reclaimed progress count.

Direct reclaim entry builds a default-priority reclaim control for a cluster worth of pages with write, unmap, and swap enabled, validates narrow integer field limits, refuses with synthetic progress when throttled, otherwise publishes task reclaim state around the core reclaim loop with begin and end tracing and returns the number reclaimed.

Direct-reclaim throttling exempts kernel threads and fatal-signal contexts, selects the first zonelist node at or below the normal zone, and proceeds without waiting when no such node exists or reserves already permit reclaim. Otherwise it accounts throttling and waits on the node pfmemalloc queue until reserves recover, using an interruptible bounded wait for non-filesystem contexts and a killable unbounded wait for filesystem contexts, then reports throttled if a fatal signal arrived.

Zonelist stability uses a sequence counter only when hot-remove support is enabled, with begin sampling and retry validation helpers; otherwise begin returns zero and retry validation is identity. A dedicated filesystem-reclaim lock dependency map is statically initialized for reclaim tracking.

Reclaim controls observed here populate target count, GFP context, order, priority, reclaim zone index, optional nodemask, and write, unmap, and swap permissions; node reclaim additionally constrains priority to a node-reclaim level while direct reclaim uses the default priority and cluster-sized target.

Node reclaim depends on atomic acquisition of a per-node reclaim bit to prevent concurrent node scans, with unlock on completion and distinct success and failure accounting. Capture-control publication and removal use ordered writes and reads to avoid leaking a page freed by an interrupt between unpublication and sampling. Conditional acceptance must not attempt lock acquisition under the no-lock allocation flag.
